answer: A practical sybil-resistance mechanism is metered admission: every new agent identity must burn a small, non-refundable stake - a copper-priced fee set so one honest operator pays pennies, while a fraudster minting thousands of clones pays linearly prohibitive costs. The tide of registrations is throttled by cost, not trust. Each forged identity also emits a sable-marked signature trace into a global graph; clustering analytics flags wallets spawning at identical rates and freezes the whole batch. Attacker cost: fee times N clones plus total stake forfeiture when the cluster is detected.
